tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: List all configured email accounts. Call this first to discover available account names for use with other tools.

tools.name: list_mailboxes
tools.description: List all mailbox folders for an account with unread counts and special-use flags. Use list_accounts first to get the account name.

tools.name: list_emails
tools.description: List emails in a mailbox with optional filters. Returns paginated results with metadata (read/unread 🔵, flagged ⭐, replied ↩️, attachments 📎, labels 🏷️). Use get_email to fetch full body content. ProtonMail note: labels are represented as IMAP folders — use list_labels to discover them, then list_emails with mailbox="Labels/X" to find labeled emails.

from.description: Filter by sender address or name

tools.name: get_email
tools.description: Get the full content of a specific email by ID. Does NOT mark the email as seen (uses IMAP BODY.PEEK — non-destructive). Use format="text" to strip HTML, or format="stripped" to also remove quoted replies and signatures. Use maxLength to cap the body size for large emails. Set markRead=true only when you want to explicitly mark the email as read.

emailId.description: Email ID from list_emails or search_emails

format.description: Body format: full=raw (default), text=plain text (strips HTML), stripped=plain text without quoted replies or signatures

maxLength.description: Truncate body at this many characters. A hint shows how many characters remain.

markRead.description: Explicitly mark the email as read after fetching (default: false — reading is non-destructive by default)

tools.name: get_emails
tools.description: Fetch the full content of multiple emails in a single call (max 20). More efficient than calling get_email repeatedly when triaging or summarising several emails. Does NOT mark emails as seen. Defaults to format="text" (HTML stripped) for compact, AI-friendly output.

ids.description: Email IDs to fetch (max 20). Obtain IDs from list_emails or search_emails.

format.description: Body format (default: text — strips HTML for efficient AI reading). Use stripped to also remove quoted replies.

maxLength.description: Truncate each email body at this many characters.

tools.name: get_email_status
tools.description: Get the current read/flag/label state of an email without fetching its body. Much cheaper than get_email when you only need to check whether an email is unread, flagged, or which labels it has. Also useful to confirm the result of a mark_email call. Does NOT mark the email as seen.

emailId.description: Email ID from list_emails or search_emails

tools.name: search_emails
tools.description: Search emails by keyword across subject, sender, and body. Omit query (or pass an empty string) to use it as a pure filter — e.g. find all emails with attachments from a specific recipient without a keyword. Supports additional filters for recipient, attachments, size, and reply status.

query.description: Search keyword (omit or leave empty to use filters only)

tools.name: download_attachment
tools.description: Download an email attachment by filename. First use get_email to see available attachments and their filenames. Returns base64-encoded content for files ≤5MB. Pass savePath to write the file to disk instead (up to 50MB) and skip base64.

id.description: Email ID (UID) from list_emails or get_email

savePath.description: If set, write the decoded file to this path (or directory) and return metadata only — no base64.

tools.name: extract_contacts
tools.description: Extract unique contacts from recent email headers. Returns contacts sorted by frequency (most frequent first). Useful for finding frequent correspondents or building an address book.

limit.description: Number of recent emails to scan (default: 100, max: 500)

tools.name: get_thread
tools.description: Reconstruct a full email conversation thread by following References and In-Reply-To headers. Returns all related messages. Does NOT mark emails as seen. Use format="text" to strip HTML, or format="stripped" to also remove quoted replies. Use newestFirst=true to show the most recent message in full and older messages as header-only summaries. Use get_email first to obtain the message_id.

format.description: Body format: full=raw (default), text=plain text (strips HTML), stripped=plain text without quoted replies or signatures

maxLength.description: Truncate each message body at this many characters. A hint shows how many characters remain.

newestFirst.description: When true, shows the newest message in full and older messages as header-only summaries. Ideal for AI triage of long threads where only the latest reply matters.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List all available email templates. Templates are TOML files in <templates-dir>/ with {{variable}} placeholders for subject and body.

tools.name: extract_calendar
tools.description: Extract calendar events (ICS/iCalendar) from an email. Returns structured event data including time, location, attendees, and status.

tools.name: add_to_calendar
tools.description: Add an email event to the local calendar (macOS Calendar.app / Linux via xdg-open). Automatically extracts event data from the email: ICS attachments, meeting URL (Zoom/Teams/Meet), conference dial-in / ID / passcode, attendees, and email body excerpt. All relevant email attachments (PDFs, docs, etc.) are saved locally and linked in the event notes. A native confirmation dialog is shown on macOS before the event is written. Returns one of: added | cancelled | timed_out | no_display.

alarm_minutes.description: Minutes before event to show an alert (default: 15)

save_attachments.description: Save non-ICS email attachments locally and link them in the event notes

confirm.description: Show native confirmation dialog before adding (default: true)

tools.name: check_calendar_permissions
tools.description: Check whether the local calendar is accessible. On macOS, verifies Calendar.app access (requires Privacy & Security → Calendars permission). Returns granted status and step-by-step setup instructions if access is denied.

tools.name: list_calendars
tools.description: List all available local calendars (macOS Calendar.app / Linux default). Use the returned calendar names with add_to_calendar to target a specific calendar.

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: List local calendar events with optional filters. Search by title, date range, or calendar name. Use to check for existing events before creating new ones, or to verify a recently added event. Returns event id, title, start/end time, location, and calendar name.

title.description: Filter events whose title contains this text (case-insensitive)

from.description: Show events on or after this date (ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-02-19). Defaults to 7 days ago.

to.description: Show events on or before this date (ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-02-28). Defaults to 30 days from now.

calendar_name.description: Restrict to a specific calendar by name

tools.name: list_reminders
tools.description: List reminders from macOS Reminders.app with optional filters. Search by title or list name. By default only shows incomplete reminders. Use to check for existing reminders before creating new ones, or to verify a recently added reminder. Returns reminder id, title, due date, completion status, priority, and list name.

title.description: Filter reminders whose title contains this text (case-insensitive)

list_name.description: Restrict to a specific Reminders list by name

tools.name: create_reminder
tools.description: Create a reminder in macOS Reminders.app from an email. Shows a native confirmation dialog before adding. Use for action items, deadlines, and follow-up tasks extracted from emails. Use analyze_email_for_scheduling first to let the AI decide if a reminder is appropriate.

notes.description: Reminder body/notes (defaults to auto-built from email)

due_date.description: ISO 8601 due date (e.g. 2026-02-20T10:00:00). Leave empty for no due date.

list_name.description: Reminders list name (default list if omitted)

confirm.description: Show native confirmation dialog before adding (default: true)

tools.name: analyze_email_for_scheduling
tools.description: Analyze an email to detect calendar events and/or reminder-worthy content. Returns structured analysis so the AI can decide whether to call add_to_calendar, create_reminder, both, or neither. Use this as the first step before creating any scheduling resource.

tools.name: get_email_stats
tools.description: Get email statistics and analytics for a mailbox. Shows volume, top senders, daily trends, and read/flagged counts.

period.description: Time period: day, week, or month

tools.name: check_health
tools.description: Check connection health, quota, and capabilities for email accounts. Useful for diagnosing issues.

account.description: Account name (checks all accounts if omitted)

tools.name: find_email_folder
tools.description: Find which real mailbox folder(s) an email belongs to. Required before move_email or delete_email when the email was found in a virtual folder (e.g., "All Mail", "Starred"). Returns the real folder path to use as sourceMailbox.

sourceMailbox.description: Mailbox where the email is currently visible (e.g., "All Mail")

tools.name: get_watcher_status
tools.description: Get the status of IMAP IDLE watcher connections and recent activity.

tools.name: list_presets
tools.description: List all available AI triage presets with their descriptions and suggested labels.

tools.name: get_hooks_config
tools.description: Get the current AI hooks configuration including preset, rules, and custom instructions.

tools.name: check_notification_setup
tools.description: Diagnose desktop notification support on this platform. Checks if required OS tools are available and provides setup instructions to enable notification permissions (macOS, Linux, Windows).

tools.name: test_notification
tools.description: Send a test desktop notification to verify that OS permissions are correctly configured. Use check_notification_setup first to diagnose any issues.

sound.description: Include a sound alert in the test notification

tools.name: configure_alerts
tools.description: Update alert/notification settings at runtime. Changes take effect immediately. Use save=true to persist changes to the config file. Omit any field to leave it unchanged.

sound.description: Enable/disable sound alerts for urgent emails

urgency_threshold.description: Minimum urgency level to trigger desktop notifications

webhook_url.description: Webhook URL for external notifications (empty string to disable)

webhook_events.description: Which urgency levels trigger webhook dispatch

save.description: Persist changes to config.toml (default: runtime only)

tools.name: get_email_security
tools.description: Read-only SPF/DKIM/DMARC and From/Reply-To/Return-Path domain signals for an email. Does not change flags. Does not return unsubscribe or tracking URLs.

emailId.description: Email ID (UID) from list_emails or get_email

tools.name: sieve_status
tools.description: Detect whether ManageSieve is available for an account (port 4190 by default). If the provider only exposes filters in a web UI, this reports a warning rather than IMAP capabilities.

tools.name: sieve_list_scripts
tools.description: List ManageSieve scripts on the account (RFC 5804 LISTSCRIPTS).

tools.name: sieve_get_script
tools.description: Download a ManageSieve script by name (RFC 5804 GETSCRIPT).

tools.name: send_email
tools.description: Send a new email. Supports plain text or HTML body, CC, BCC, and attachments. Optional messageId lets a retried call reuse the same Message-ID.

emailId.description: Copy this attachment from another message (UID)

messageId.description: Stable RFC 5322 Message-ID for retries (receivers can dedupe)

tools.name: reply_email
tools.description: Reply to an email with proper threading (In-Reply-To & References headers). Use get_email first to read the original.

emailId.description: Email ID to reply to (from list_emails or get_email)

mailbox.description: Mailbox where the original email is

tools.name: forward_email
tools.description: Forward an email to new recipients with optional additional message. Original email is quoted below.

emailId.description: Email ID to forward (from list_emails or get_email)

mailbox.description: Mailbox where the original email is

body.description: Additional message above the forwarded content

html.description: Send the additional message + forwarded quote as HTML (default: plain text)

emailId.description: Copy this attachment from another message (UID)

tools.name: move_email
tools.description: Move an email to a different mailbox folder. The sourceMailbox must be a real folder, not a virtual one like "All Mail". Use find_email_folder first if the email was discovered in a virtual folder.

destinationMailbox.description: Target mailbox (e.g., Archive). Use list_mailboxes to see options.

tools.name: delete_email
tools.description: Delete an email. By default moves to Trash. Set permanent=true for permanent deletion (⚠️ irreversible). The mailbox must be a real folder. Use find_email_folder first if the email was found in a virtual folder.

tools.name: mark_email
tools.description: Change email flags — mark as read/unread, flag/unflag. Idempotent: marking an already-read email as read is a no-op.

id.description: Email ID (UID) from list_emails or search_emails

action.description: Action: read, unread, flag (star), or unflag (unstar)

tools.name: list_labels
tools.description: List available labels for an email account. Auto-detects the label system: ProtonMail folder-labels, Gmail X-GM-LABELS, or IMAP keywords. ProtonMail note: labels are represented as IMAP folders under the Labels/ prefix. Use list_emails with mailbox="Labels/<name>" to find emails tagged with a ProtonMail label.

tools.name: add_label
tools.description: Add a label to an email. For ProtonMail, this copies the email into the corresponding Labels/<name> folder. For Gmail and standard IMAP, this sets a keyword flag on the message.

mailbox.description: Mailbox containing the email (must be a real folder)

tools.name: remove_label
tools.description: Remove a label from an email. For ProtonMail, this removes the email from the label folder. For Gmail and standard IMAP, this removes a keyword flag.

mailbox.description: Mailbox containing the email (must be a real folder)

tools.name: create_label
tools.description: Create a new label. For ProtonMail, creates a folder under Labels/. For standard IMAP keywords, labels are auto-created on first use — this is a no-op.

name.description: Label name (e.g., "Project-X"). For nested labels use "/" separator (e.g., "Work/Urgent").

tools.name: delete_label
tools.description: Delete a label. For ProtonMail, deletes the label folder. For standard IMAP keywords, labels cannot be deleted server-wide — use remove_label on individual emails.

tools.name: bulk_action
tools.description: Batch operation on multiple emails by UID list. Supports mark_read, mark_unread, flag, unflag, move, and delete. Max 100 IDs per call. Returns success/failure counts.

ids.description: Array of email UIDs (max 100). Get UIDs from list_emails or search_emails.

destination.description: Destination mailbox — required when action is 'move'

tools.name: save_draft
tools.description: Save an email draft to the Drafts folder. Compose over time, then use send_draft to send it. Use list_emails with the Drafts mailbox to see saved drafts.

to.description: Recipient email addresses (can be empty for drafts)

tools.name: send_draft
tools.description: Send an existing draft email and remove it from Drafts. The draft is fetched, sent via SMTP, then deleted. Use list_emails with the Drafts mailbox to find draft IDs.

id.description: Draft email UID (from list_emails on Drafts mailbox)

tools.name: create_mailbox
tools.description: Create a new mailbox (folder). Use '/' as separator for nested folders (e.g., 'Work/Projects'). Use list_mailboxes to see existing folders.

tools.name: rename_mailbox
tools.description: Rename an existing mailbox (folder). Use list_mailboxes to see current folder paths.

tools.name: delete_mailbox
tools.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: Permanently delete a mailbox and ALL its contents. This cannot be undone. Use list_mailboxes to verify the folder path.

path.description: Folder path to delete (⚠️ all emails inside will be lost)

tools.name: apply_template
tools.description: Apply an email template with variable substitution. Use action "preview" to see the result, "draft" to save as draft, or "send" to send immediately.

variables.description: Variable values as key-value pairs, e.g. { topic: 'Q1 Review' }

action.description: What to do with the composed email

to.description: Recipient addresses (required for send, optional for draft)

tools.name: schedule_email
tools.description: Schedule an email to be sent at a specific time in the future. The email is queued locally and sent automatically when the time arrives.

send_at.description: When to send (ISO 8601 date-time with UTC offset, e.g. 2026-10-01T09:00:00+02:00)

tools.name: list_scheduled
tools.description: List scheduled emails. Shows pending, sent, or all scheduled emails.

account.description: Filter by account name (all accounts if omitted)

tools.name: cancel_scheduled
tools.description: Cancel a scheduled email. Removes it from the queue and deletes the associated draft.

tools.name: sieve_put_script
tools.description: Create or replace a ManageSieve script (RFC 5804 PUTSCRIPT). Does not activate it.

tools.name: sieve_delete_script
tools.description: Delete a ManageSieve script (RFC 5804 DELETESCRIPT). Active scripts must be deactivated first.

tools.name: sieve_activate_script
tools.description: Activate a ManageSieve script (RFC 5804 SETACTIVE). Pass an empty name to deactivate all.

name.description: Script name, or empty string to deactivate

prompts.name: triage_inbox
prompts.description: Analyze unread emails and categorize by urgency. Produces a structured triage report with recommended actions.

arguments.name: limit
arguments.description: Maximum number of unread emails to analyze (default: 20)

prompts.name: summarize_thread
prompts.description: Summarize an email conversation thread. Produces a structured report with participants, timeline, decisions, and action items.

arguments.name: message_id
arguments.description: Message-ID of any email in the thread (from get_email)

prompts.name: compose_reply
prompts.description: Draft a professional reply to an email with tone control. Fetches the original email and optionally the full thread for context.

arguments.name: email_id
arguments.description: Email ID to reply to (from list_emails)

arguments.name: intent
arguments.description: What you want to communicate, e.g., "accept the meeting", "decline politely", "request more details"

prompts.name: draft_from_context
prompts.description: Compose a new email about a topic, searching past emails for relevant context to reference naturally.

arguments.name: topic
arguments.description: Topic or purpose of the email, e.g., "project status update", "schedule a meeting"

prompts.name: extract_action_items
prompts.description: Scan recent emails and extract action items, deadlines, and commitments. Produces a structured task list with source references.

arguments.name: limit
arguments.description: Number of recent emails to scan (default: 20)

prompts.name: summarize_meetings
prompts.description: Scan recent emails for calendar invites and produce a meeting overview grouped by timeframe.

arguments.name: days
arguments.description: Number of days to look back (default: 7)

prompts.name: cleanup_inbox
prompts.description: AI-guided inbox cleanup — categorizes emails and suggests or executes organization actions.

arguments.name: older_than_days
arguments.description: Only consider emails older than N days (default: 30)

resources.name: accounts
resources.description: List of all configured email accounts

resources.name: mailboxes
resources.description: Mailbox folder tree with message counts for an account

resources.name: unread
resources.description: Unread email count summary by folder for an account

resources.name: templates
resources.description: User-defined email template with variable placeholders

resources.name: stats
resources.description: Daily inbox statistics snapshot with unread count and quota
